h1.text: On January 1st, 2027, California bans Red No. 3 in food, with no sell-through period.

h2.text: This is a simulated compliance drill on 20 California Walmart and Sam's Club locations, where the dye hides under names like erythrosine and E127.

h3.text: You'll see a working system that Gemini 4 Argon wrote this morning, in one generation.

c1.text: Here's the drill. We run the core on all 20 stores: 13,746 shelf tasks, replayed overnight against the midnight deadline. Each dot turns green when its store is done.

c2.text: Click a Supercenter and you're inside it. Flashing tags are pulls still pending. Associates walk to each facing, pull the product, and place a substitute.

c3.text: Every verdict carries its evidence. Erythrosine: caught and pulled. A vague "artificial color": held to verify. A Red 40 decoy: kept on the shelf.

c4.text: Then the verifier. Argon's unedited core: 350 hard errors, and recall 0.947. It missed 25 products spelled like "F D and C" with spaces, or Spanish "rojo".

c5.text: After 3 small logged patches: 0 hard errors, recall 1.0, precision 0.998, and 0 of 483 decoys pulled.

c6.text: Stores, stock and staffing are simulated. Every number came from the verifier.

f_h3_exp1.text: You'll see a working system Argon wrote this morning, and an experiment where Argon wrote a 254,377-token version in one continued generation.

f_c4.text: Argon's unedited core: 350 hard errors, recall 0.947. After 3 small logged patches: 0 hard errors, recall 1.0, precision 0.998, 0 of 483 decoys pulled.

f_e1_exp1.text: The experiment: one continued generation over 4 hops, 254,377 visible tokens in 33.8 minutes, about $3.56. Seams, where one hop hands off mid-file: 3 of 3 pass.

f_e2_exp1.text: The code wall puts every file at its token position. All 2,838 cross-file references resolve. The longest passing call: ids.py at token 36,357, used by a test at token 249,087.

f_e3_exp1.text: We run both files' tests live. They pass.

f_e4_exp1.text: What broke as length grew: 3 failing test files in the first 200 thousand tokens, 1 after, and 149 status strings outside the contract's enums.

f_e5.text: A managed repair agent takes failing files: the core's pack_returns went to 7 of 7 passing in 96 seconds. On fresh package B's rules, round two cut failures from 32 to 1, fixed 15 of 16 held-out cases, with 0 new failures.

f_e6.text: Matched packages, same hidden tests. Rules written in-stream pass 1,143 of 1,254; written fresh, 1,240. Allocate: both 9 of 9.

f_w1.text: RAG plus code is the right way to run a compliance pull, and it's what Argon wrote. We tested whether one long generation can write it coherently, and you've just seen where it held and where it broke.

f_x1.text: For compliance teams at any big retailer. Stores, stock and staffing are simulated, and every number came from the verifier. Open source.
